data.registration_trigger: Recording of a Notice of Default (NOD) on a residential property; continues through REO.
data.who_must_register: Beneficiary or trustee with an interest in the deed of trust (lender/servicer).
data.registration_deadline: Within 30 days of the recording of the Notice of Default.
data.ordinance_name: LAMC Ch. XVI Art. 4 Sec. 164.00 et seq. - Foreclosure Registry Program (Ord. 181185, amended Ord. 183281 and 187627)
data.registration_fee: $155 annual registration fee (non-refundable, paid at registration; one law firm reports $160 incl. 2.49% admin fee). Separate $356 proactive inspection fee when the property moves from NOD to REO.
data.renewal_frequency: Annual while the property remains subject to the registry
documents_required: Online registration on the LAHD Foreclosure Registry website
Beneficiary and trustee names and contact information
Local property management company / responsible contact
other_requirements: Maintain the property (LA ordinance requires lenders to maintain and repair vacant foreclosed residential property)
Pay the $356 proactive inspection fee when the property becomes REO
Request de-registration within 10 calendar days after the property is no longer subject to the registry (NOD cancelled or property sold)
data.penalties: Administrative penalties for failure to register (appeal form available from LAHD).
data.contact_info: Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) Foreclosure Registry Program
data.summary: Los Angeles requires lenders (beneficiary/trustee) to register residential properties with LAHD within 30 days after a Notice of Default is recorded, pay a $155 annual fee, pay a $356 inspection fee at REO, maintain the property, and de-register within 10 days when it no longer qualifies.
data.confidence_reason: Confirmed on LAHD program pages and ordinance documents.

data.registration_trigger: Building becomes vacant (DOB guidance refers to properties vacant/unoccupied 90 days or more; the statute text says within 30 days after it becomes vacant).
data.registration_deadline: Statute (D.C. Code 42-3131.06(a)): within 30 days after the building becomes vacant; the Mayor may extend for good cause.
data.ordinance_name: D.C. Code Sec. 42-3131.06 (registration of vacant buildings) and 42-3131.09 (fees)
data.registration_fee: $350 registration fee per DOB's March 2026 Vacant Building Response Form (older code versions show $250 initial / $250 renewal).
data.renewal_fee: Unconfirmed ($250 in older code text; one source lists $500)
documents_required: Account in DOB's online Vacant Building Enforcement system
Registration fee payment through the DOB online payment portal
Arrangement for an inspection of the building at the time of initial registration
Exemption documentation if claiming an exemption (e.g. government-owned, hardship such as a significant medical event)
other_requirements: Maintain the building to the standards of D.C. Code 42-3131.12
Report any change in owner name or address within 30 days
data.penalties: Vacant and blighted properties are taxed at higher Class 3/Class 4 real property tax rates; fines for failure to register.
data.summary: Washington, DC requires owners of vacant buildings to register with the Department of Buildings through its online Vacant Building Enforcement system, pay the registration fee ($350 on the 2026 DOB form) and arrange an inspection. DC is an independent federal district, so no separate state or county requirements apply.
data.confidence_reason: Statute and DOB pages confirm the requirement; the deadline (30 vs 90 days) and current fee conflict between sources.

data.registration_trigger: Mortgage in default, property vacant, or property in foreclosure (each property registered separately, vacant or occupied).
data.who_must_register: Mortgagee holding a mortgage on real property in the City of Jacksonville.
data.registration_deadline: Inspect upon default/before issuing a notice of default; register per Chapter 179 (exact days not confirmed).
data.ordinance_name: Jacksonville Ordinance Code Title VI, Ch. 179 - Foreclosed Property Registry (amended by Ord. 2018-104-E)
data.registration_fee: Set in Sec. 179.104(e) / city fee schedule (a 2010 version charged $150; current amount not confirmed).
documents_required: Local property manager / responsible party contact
Default / foreclosure status and inspection results
other_requirements: Mortgagee must inspect the property upon default or before issuing a notice of default
data.contact_info: City of Jacksonville Neighborhoods Department - Foreclosed Property Registry
data.summary: Jacksonville (Ch. 179, amended 2018) requires mortgagees to register every property whose mortgage is in default, that is vacant, or that is in foreclosure, inspect on default, and renew annually; the current fee is in Sec. 179.104(e).
data.confidence_reason: Requirement confirmed on the city's registry page; current fee amount not confirmed.

data.registration_trigger: Vacant 30+ days - but only for vacant lots over 10,000 sq ft, non-residential structures and residential properties with 50 or more units.
data.who_must_register: Owner (out-of-state owners must designate an in-state agent).
data.ordinance_name: Phoenix City Code Ch. 39, Art. IX, Secs. 39-49 to 39-55 - Vacant Property Registry (Ord. G-7203, eff. 1/12/2024)
documents_required: Street address and Maricopa County Assessor parcel number
Owner name, address, email and telephone
Agent name and contact details (in-state agent required for out-of-state owners)
other_requirements: Remove the property from the registry when no longer vacant
data.penalties: $500 minimum for a first violation (fines reported from $500 to $2,500).
data.contact_info: City of Phoenix Neighborhood Services Department - myPHX311
data.summary: Phoenix's Vacant Property Registry (2024) covers only vacant lots over 10,000 sq ft, non-residential buildings and residential properties with 50+ units, vacant 30+ days; registration is free online. Typical 1-4 unit homes are NOT covered, so no registration is required for them.
data.confidence_reason: Scope confirmed on the city page and news coverage. NOTE: operator records marked Phoenix 'Yes' - review whether operators register single-family homes here.

data.registration_trigger: Residential property that is vacant/abandoned, including properties in foreclosure.
data.who_must_register: Beneficiary / lender or owner of the abandoned residential property.
data.ordinance_name: Aurora City Code - Abandoned/vacant residential property registration
data.registration_fee: Annual fee per property, adjusted each January 1 ($68.75 for 2026 per city materials); not prorated.
data.renewal_frequency: Annual - due January 1, must be received by January 31
documents_required: Beneficiary/owner name and direct street mailing address (no P.O. boxes)
Direct contact name and phone number
Local property management / asset management company responsible for security and maintenance
data.contact_info: City of Aurora - Vacant/abandoned property registration
data.summary: Aurora requires registration of vacant/abandoned residential properties (including those in foreclosure) online or by mail-in form, with an annual per-property fee adjusted every January 1 ($68.75 in 2026).
data.confidence_reason: City registration portal and mail-in form confirmed; fee amount from city materials surfaced in search.

data.registration_trigger: Property vacant 90 continuous days, or 180 non-continuous days within a year.
data.ordinance_name: Pueblo Municipal Code - vacant property registration
data.summary: Pueblo requires owners to register properties vacant 90 continuous days (or 180 non-continuous days in a year), $500 per year, renewing every January 1.
data.confidence_reason: From an industry ordinance tracker and consistent with operator records; city code text not accessible.

data.registration_trigger: Building unoccupied for more than three consecutive months.
data.who_must_register: Owner (the City may also register a property after inspection).
data.registration_deadline: Within 30 days after the building becomes vacant.
data.ordinance_name: Dover Code of Ordinances Ch. 22 (Buildings and building regulations) - vacant building registration
documents_required: City of Dover vacant building registration form
Registration fee per city fee schedule
other_requirements: Secure and maintain the vacant building
data.summary: Dover requires owners to register any building unoccupied more than three consecutive months with Planning & Inspections within 30 days of vacancy, using the city's vacant building form.
data.confidence_reason: Requirement confirmed from city ordinance text and form; fee amount not confirmed.

data.ordinance_name: Town of Smyrna vacant building registration
documents_required: Town of Smyrna Vacant Building Registration Form
data.contact_info: Town of Smyrna, 27 South Market Street Plaza, P.O. Box 307, Smyrna, DE 19977
data.summary: Smyrna publishes a Vacant Building Registration Form for vacant buildings; trigger and fee were not confirmed.
data.confidence_reason: Only the town's form was found; ordinance text not accessible.

data.registration_trigger: Building becomes vacant or is deemed vacant; beneficiary requirements for properties in default (HMC 14-503).
data.who_must_register: Owner of the vacant building; beneficiary for properties in default.
data.registration_deadline: Within 10 days of the building becoming vacant or being deemed vacant.
data.ordinance_name: Hemet Municipal Code Ch. 14, Art. XI, Secs. 14-501 to 14-511 (amended Oct. 10, 2023)
documents_required: City of Hemet vacant property registration form
Owner / beneficiary name, address and phone
data.contact_info: City of Hemet Department of Life Safety, Code Compliance Division - (951) 765-2339
data.summary: Hemet requires owners of vacant buildings (and beneficiaries of properties in default) to register with Code Compliance within 10 days of vacancy; $420 initial and $168 annual renewal.
data.confidence_reason: City forms and guidelines confirm; fee amounts differ slightly between form versions.

data.registration_trigger: Vacant building; and properties found vacant after a default (beneficiary/trustee registration).
data.who_must_register: Owner of a vacant building; beneficiary or trustee of a defaulted property found vacant.
data.ordinance_name: Modesto Municipal Code - vacant building / property registration
documents_required: Owner / beneficiary / trustee name and contact information
other_requirements: Post a 'No Trespassing' sign on the property frontage, at least 17 x 22 inches
data.summary: Modesto requires registration of vacant buildings and of defaulted properties found vacant (by the beneficiary/trustee) within 10 days of vacancy, $238 per year, with security and signage requirements.
data.confidence_reason: From an industry tracker and a code summary site; city code text not accessible.

data.registration_trigger: Vacant/abandoned property, including property in default or foreclosure.
data.who_must_register: Deed-of-trust holder (lender) for properties in default/foreclosure, and owners of vacant property.
data.ordinance_name: Palmdale Municipal Code Ch. 8.38 - Vacant and Abandoned Property Registration
data.registration_fee: $366.50 per property per year (set by City Council resolution).
documents_required: Lender / owner name and contact information
data.summary: Palmdale (Ch. 8.38) requires registration of vacant and abandoned properties, including properties in default or foreclosure by the deed-of-trust holder; annual fee $366.50 per property.
data.confidence_reason: Chapter confirmed; fee from an industry tracker.

data.registration_trigger: Residential property in default (Notice of Default recorded).
data.ordinance_name: Moreno Valley foreclosure/vacant residential property registration program
data.registration_fee: $400 registration fee, submitted with the Notice of Default information.
documents_required: Copy of the Notice of Default
data.contact_info: City of Moreno Valley Community Development - Code & Neighborhood Services
data.summary: Moreno Valley requires registration of residential properties in default, with a $400 fee sent along with the Notice of Default.
data.confidence_reason: From the city's foreclosure program information sheet.

data.ordinance_name: City of Perris abandoned/foreclosed residential property registration
data.summary: Perris requires registration of abandoned/foreclosed residential properties using the city form; $130 fee.
data.confidence_reason: From the city's registration form.

data.summary: Indio's Code Enforcement runs a foreclosure registration program for defaulted/vacant residential properties; the renewal form lists a $100 fee.
data.confidence_reason: From city program page and form.

data.registration_trigger: Vacant residential property under a current Notice of Default or Notice of Trustee's Sale.
data.ordinance_name: Riverside County Ordinance No. 881 - Abandoned/vacant residential property registration
data.renewal_frequency: Annual - registration valid for the calendar year in which it is made
other_requirements: California county ordinances apply only in unincorporated territory.
data.summary: Unincorporated Riverside County requires registration of vacant residential properties under a Notice of Default or Trustee's Sale (Ord. 881), $70 per calendar year. California county ordinances apply only in unincorporated territory.
data.confidence_reason: From the county code enforcement registration form.

data.registration_trigger: Distressed property: vacant real property in foreclosure, or vacant real property with a hazardous condition (on county notice).
data.who_must_register: Responsible parties (owner / mortgagee) of the distressed property.
data.ordinance_name: Jefferson County Distressed Real Properties Ordinance
documents_required: County registration for vacant property in foreclosure
other_requirements: County ordinances apply in unincorporated Jefferson County, not inside cities such as Arvada or Lakewood.
data.summary: Unincorporated Jefferson County requires registration of vacant real property in foreclosure and, on written notice, other vacant property with a hazardous condition (Distressed Real Properties Ordinance).
data.confidence_reason: County ordinance confirmed; fee not confirmed.
